digest.component_or_area: LLM provider integration layer (Bedrock native support)
propositions: Rebar lacks a first-class Bedrock provider, forcing operators to use an OpenAI-compatible gateway that sacrifices prompt caching, native structured output, and the retrying transport.

Bedrock inference profiles support prompt caching (measured: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 cache_write=4017 then cache_read=4017), but some models (us./global. opus-4-5) silently fail to cache while billing full input tokens with no error signal.

Bedrock silently rejects the temperature parameter on some models (us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 returns 400 ValidationException), breaking rebar's Pass-2 verify gates that deliberately send temperature=0 for determinism, whereas the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully.

A new cache-ineffectiveness warning predicate must fire when caching was requested but both cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens are zero despite input_tokens>0, to alert operators to silent full-price billing.

The model-id-specific capability override table (_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES) must be separate from f184's profile-shaped (_REBAR_OVERRIDES) to avoid breaching its closed contract while still withdrawing temperature from affected Bedrock models only.

A provider-agnostic error translator in failure.py must catch 400 ValidationException messages naming a sampling parameter and a rejection word, converting them to actionable LLMConfigError rather than swallowing unrelated 400s.
